transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-01-21
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Arielle Stone (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Nina Patel (Meridian Head of Platform), Carlos Ruiz (Meridian Security Lead), Jules Park (Meridian Procurement), Samir Khatri (Meridian DevOps)

Summary:
Quick procurement + security alignment to unblock staging access and agree an SLA baseline for the pilot. Discussed MSA/DPA redlines, KMS/SSO options, egress/egress billing expectations, and a short performance run on dedicated capacity. Action items and dates at the bottom.

Topics (auto): MSA redlines, DPA data residency, SLA targets and rollback, staging network, KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML, pilot timeline, pricing approval path

[00:00] Arielle: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we've got about 45 minutes, is that right?
[00:06] Nina: Yep, that works for us. We're juggling a procurement review this week so appreciate the focused agenda.
[00:12] Arielle: Great. Quick intro — I'm Arielle on AE side, Marcus is our SE who will lead the staging and perf work. 
[00:18] Marcus: Hi all, thanks. I'll be talking infra and the dedicated pool options.
[00:23] Jules: Jules here from procurement — I'll be tracking the MSA/DPA redlines and timeline.
[00:26] Samir: Samir, DevOps — I'll need the network/egress details and staging creds.
[00:30] Carlos: Carlos from security, I'll focus on KMS, SSO and audit log expectations.

[02:10] Arielle: To start, high level ask from Meridian is a 4‑week pilot on a dedicated pool with strict data isolation and a contract path that gets to procurement approval by end of month. Is that still the ask?
[02:22] Nina: Yes, the business needs to validate latency and throughput with our payment flows. Also legal needs the DPA to confirm no cross‑region data movement for PNII during the pilot.
[02:34] Arielle: Understood. On data residency we can support region pinning in Redwood Private or our Dedicated offering with VPC peering; for hosted we have configs but it's trickier for strict no‑export. Marcus, quick note?
[02:46] Marcus: Yeah, for the dedicated pool we can pin to our eu‑west‑2 region or us‑west‑1, and we can disable cross‑region replica for the KV cache. That said some tooling (metrics) route through our telemetry endpoint, we have an option to send logs to your S3 or to a customer‑managed endpoint — depends on DPA wording.

[05:03] Carlos: Important — we require customer‑managed KMS for encryption at rest during the pilot, or at least a Bring‑Your‑Own‑Key option. We also need rotatable keys and HSM backed if possible.
[05:15] Marcus: BYOK is supported on Private and Dedicated with an HSM flow; on hosted it's a managed KMS but we can negotiate key escrow/rotations in the DPA. There may be a premium for escrow but we can document the tradeoff.

[07:12] Jules: On the MSA redlines — there are three ask boxes from procurement: 1) liability cap aligned with our vendor policy, 2) right to audit for the first 90 days, and 3) data breach notification SLA of 48 hours. How flexible is Redwood on those?
[07:27] Arielle: We're open but need to reconcile with our platform insurance. Liability cap — typically we try to avoid unlimited exposure, we can discuss a mid‑range cap tied to annual contract value. Right to audit is something we accommodate with scoped security reviews. Notification SLA 48 hours is aggressive but we can commit to 72 hours as a baseline and escalate for enterprise customers.
[07:45] Nina: 72 is a little long for payments, can we commit to 48 for the pilot and then 72 for normal production?
[07:50] Arielle: I can take that back to legal — put it in the redline sheet as a pilot exception request.

[09:30] Samir: For staging access, do you provide bastion hosts or do we need to open ports into our VPC? Network diagram would help so we can run firewall rules.
[09:38] Marcus: We typically offer three flows: 1) VPC peering, 2) PrivateLink endpoints, 3) temporary SSH bastion for admin tasks. For the pilot I'd recommend PrivateLink + per‑route RBAC so you don't expose things unnecessarily. We'll share a ports checklist.

[11:05] Carlos: Also need full audit logs for every request with token‑level tracing and retention for at least 90 days during pilot. Can you confirm log retention policies and export formats?
[11:14] Marcus: Logs are available via our console with export to S3 in JSON or to your SIEM via syslog. Retention defaults to 30 days on hosted but for dedicated we can increase to 90 for the pilot. We'll include the export manifest link in the deck.

[13:40] Jules: Pricing question — the procurement board wants a clear estimate for a 4‑week dedicated pilot. Can you provide an itemized estimate for reserved capacity plus egress costs? We need it for budget approval.
[13:53] Arielle: Yes, we can provide a week‑by‑week burn estimate. Preview: dedicated reserved pool with three GPUs for the pilot, estimated token throughput 200k tokens/day, egress estimate depends on your payload sizes but we'll model with your sample dataset. I'll attach a spreadsheet after.

[15:22] Nina: On SLAs — we need sub‑200ms p95 for simple prompt generation flows, with failover if a pool is degraded. Do you have documented latency SLAs for dedicated?
[15:31] Marcus: Our Dedicated SLA targets p95 under 250ms for short sequences (<128 tokens) under the committed throughput. We can commit to a p95 of 200ms as a pilot target if we control placement and traffic shaping. We'll document fallback to a smaller, lower cost model in the runbook for graceful degradation.

[17:55] Carlos: About third‑party subprocessors — the DPA needs a list of subprocessors and whether they have access to plaintext data. We flagged concern over analytics providers.
[18:06] Arielle: We'll provide the subprocessors list in the DPA addendum. For the pilot, telemetry will be scoped and we can route it to your SIEM so analytics vendors don't receive plaintext. We'll mark that in the DPA.

[20:30] Samir: We'll also need an approach for token masking and redaction in transit, especially for payment PANs. Is there a recommended pattern?
[20:38] Marcus: We recommend client‑side tokenization before sending to Redwood, and we can also configure prefix filters and KV cache obfuscation. For payments, PII should be tokenized at source. We'll share our recommended pattern and a sample middleware snippet.

[22:55] Jules: Procurement has a gating question — are you compliant with SOC2 Type II? We need the latest report and Loom for security posture.
[23:04] Arielle: Yes, SOC2 Type II is available — I will share the attestation and the security pack after the call. Also our ISO27001 cert references are in the data room.

[24:40] Nina: One more governance ask — can we have a 30‑day termination clause for the pilot with data purge assurances? We need a clear path to destroy tokens and logs.
[24:50] Arielle: We can include a pilot termination clause with data purge steps — we'll outline the purge timeline and confirm S3 snapshot deletion protocols.

[26:12] Marcus: Quick technical callout: if you plan to do high concurrency tests, please avoid very long sequences during bench runs — the runtime's batching behavior changes cost and latency. We'll share a perf plan but the 48h run should include a mixed sequence length profile matching your traffic.

[28:30] Carlos: On SSO — we use SAML with IdP enforced MFA. How flexible is login for your console and staging endpoints?
[28:38] Arielle: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning; for the pilot we can set up a scoped service account and SAML enforcement for admins. Marcus will run the SAML flow setup with Samir.

[30:45] Samir: Any network egress fees from Redwood side we should expect? We want to avoid surprise cloud egress charging.
[30:54] Arielle: Egress bills depend on carrier and region; for dedicated pilots we often include a modest egress credit in the trial quote. I'll note a line item in the sheet and mark what we cover vs what Meridian covers.

[33:12] Jules: On commercial path — if pilot meets perf/SLAs, we want a 12‑month reserved contract with stepped discounts. Is that available?
[33:20] Arielle: Yes, reserved capacity discounts are standard; we can put a draft term sheet with commitment tiers. We'll include financial modeling in the spreadsheet.

[35:45] Nina: For legal redlines, can Redwood accept an audit window rather than continuous monitoring? Procurement prefers scheduled audits with a narrow scope.
[35:55] Arielle: We can agree scheduled audits plus ad‑hoc under specific cause. We'll capture that as a redline option.

[37:10] Marcus: Also wanted to note a small compatibility item — if you use an internal KMS like HashiCorp Vault, the rotation window needs to be coordinated with our agents to avoid cache miss storms. We'll document rotation best practices.

[38:50] Carlos: Do you have a defined incident response retainer or SLT for priority incidents? We need a named escalation path in the SLA.
[38:58] Arielle: We provide P1/P0 escalation contacts for enterprise customers and a named oncall for Dedicated. We'll include the contact matrix in the SLA addendum.

[41:02] Marcus: For the performance bench week of 2025‑01‑27, we'll need a staging endpoint, a service account, and the sample payloads. Samir, can you confirm you'll provide sample traffic by 2025‑01‑24?
[41:13] Samir: Yes, I can get sample payloads and the expected concurrency matrix by Friday the 24th.

[42:30] Arielle: Recap — action items: we'll send MSA/DPA redlines, security pack, pricing spreadsheet, and staging network diagram. Customer provides sample payloads, KMS details, and procurement intake form. Schedule a security deep dive next Tuesday.

[43:02] Nina: That sounds good. Any outstanding blockers from Redwood?
[43:07] Arielle: Nothing major — just legal review for the 48‑hour breach notification exception and KMS escrow pricing if we can't support BYOK on hosted.

[44:20] Jules: Timeline check — procurement needs final numbers to present at Monday's committee. Can Redwood get the cost spreadsheet and redlines by Friday 24th?
[44:30] Arielle: Yes, we'll prioritize those items and flag any commercial asks.

[45:50] Carlos: Quick note: we'll expect the SOC2 report and subprocessors list before the security deep dive.
[45:58] Arielle: Agreed — I'll share the security pack and subprocessor list in the data room link.

[47:10] Arielle: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the attachments and a calendar invite for the 01‑28 security session.
[47:18] Nina: Thanks.

End of call.
